planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this award-winning selection keeps its purple-blotched pattern best out of direct afternoon sun.

directions: Each light green, maple-shaped leaf of 'Tiger Stripe' is boldly blotched and striped with purple along purplish veins, giving the clump a distinctly patterned look even before the foamy white to pale pink flower spikes rise above the foliage in spring. This selection won a Silver Medal at the 1996 VKC NIEUW trials in Belgium. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction valued for its heavy spring bloom.

directions: 'Inkblot' produces leaves that are less finely cut than many foamflower cultivars, each marked with a bold, solid dark blotch filling the leaf center. Masses of pink-tinted white flower spikes cover the clump in spring. Keep soil consistently moist in partial to full shade and divide every few years to maintain a tidy, well-filled clump.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled to full shade; foliage color is most pronounced with some bright indirect light.

directions: Originating as a seedling found on a Dan Hinkley plant-collecting trip to Yunnan, China, 'Heronswood Mist' is a semi-evergreen foamflower with striking burgundy, chartreuse, and white variegated foliage. Airy spikes of cream and pink flowers rise above the clump in spring. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in dappled shade and divide congested clumps every few years.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; its running habit fills in moist shaded ground quickly.

directions: Discovered by Jim Plyler of Natural Landscapes Nursery, 'Slick Rock' is a vigorously running selection of the native foamflower that spreads readily by stolons to form an effective groundcover in consistently moist, shaded ground. Airy white flower spikes rise above the lobed, maple-like leaves in spring. Combines well with ferns and hostas as a low, spreading companion in a woodland shade garden.

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a compact Terra Nova Nurseries introduction (patented) suited to small spaces.

directions: 'Mystic Mist' forms a low, 5-inch clump of white-frosted, maple-shaped leaves highlighted by wide, dark purple central veins, topped by short bottlebrush spikes of white flowers in early spring. It is the earlier Terra Nova introduction that the more vigorously patterned 'Majestic Mist' was later bred to improve upon. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade and divide every few years to maintain a tidy clump.

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; running habit fills in beds within a couple of seasons.

directions: 'Dark Eyes' is a running foamflower cultivar with deep-green, maple-shaped leaves marked by a bold black-burgundy blotch at the center of each leaf. Notably large light-pink flower spikes appear in spring and often rebloom later in the season. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; avoid afternoon sun, which causes rapid leaf scorch.

directions: Also sold under its original Dutch name 'Zuster Theresa,' this early-summer-blooming arendsii hybrid bears soft, cotton-candy-pink plumes above fine, dark green, fern-like foliage. It forms a full, even mound well suited to a mixed shade border. Keep soil consistently moist and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; well suited to small beds, rock gardens, and containers.

directions: A dwarf member of the crispa group, 'Perkeo' forms a compact mound of dark, finely cut, distinctively crinkled (crispa) foliage topped by short, plume-like pink flower spikes that age toward purple in mid-to-early summer. Its small scale makes it a good fit for the front of a shaded border or a container near water. Keep soil consistently moist and divide every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; blooms later in the season than most arendsii hybrids, extending the astilbe display into late summer.

directions: 'Serenade' bears neat, conical plumes of rose-pink flowers on dark red stems above glossy, deep green, lacy, divided foliage, blooming in mid-to-late summer after most arendsii hybrids have finished. Like other chinensis selections it tolerates somewhat drier soil than Arendsii-type astilbes, though it still performs best with consistent moisture. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain dense, well-colored plumes.

planting.note: Plant divisions in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; japonica types decline quickly if allowed to dry out.

directions: 'Lollipop' bears sweet pink flower plumes on strikingly dark purple upright stems, held above a compact, bushy mound of lush, glossy dark green foliage. Its tidy habit and dark stems make the flower spikes stand out well against the foliage in a mixed shade border, and the blooms hold up well in cut arrangements. Keep soil evenly moist in partial to full shade and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
